english: Let $\theta$ be the acute angle between the two tangents drawn from the point $P(4,4)$ to the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{10}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$. Then the value of $\tan\theta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि बिन्दु $P(4,4)$ से दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{10}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{6}=1$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाओं के बीच का न्यून कोण $\theta$ है। तब $\tan\theta$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $S_1=\dfrac{16}{10}+\dfrac{16}{6}-1=\dfrac{24+40-15}{15}=\dfrac{49}{15}>0$, so $P$ is outside and two tangents exist.

Slopes of the tangents from $P$: $y=mx+(4-4m)$ touches the ellipse iff $(4-4m)^{2}=10m^{2}+6$, i.e. $6m^{2}-32m+10=0$, or $3m^{2}-16m+5=0$; so $m_1+m_2=\dfrac{16}{3}$, $m_1m_2=\dfrac53$ (no tangent is vertical, as $16\ne10$).

Equivalently, the pair of tangents is $SS_1=T^{2}$ with $T=\dfrac{4x}{10}+\dfrac{4y}{6}-1$; its second-degree part is $Ax^{2}+2Hxy+By^{2}$ with $A=\dfrac{49}{150}-\dfrac{16}{100}=\dfrac16$, $B=\dfrac{49}{90}-\dfrac{16}{36}=\dfrac{1}{10}$, $H=-\dfrac{4}{15}$. The lines through $P$ are parallel to $Ax^{2}+2Hxy+By^{2}=0$, so their slopes satisfy $Bm^{2}+2Hm+A=0$, i.e. $3m^{2}-16m+5=0$, agreeing with the direct computation.
Since $1+m_1m_2>0$, the angle given by this value is acute, so $\tan\theta=1.75$. (Same value from $\dfrac{2\sqrt{H^{2}-AB}}{|A+B|}=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac{7}{30}}{\frac{4}{15}}$.)
originality_note: New: the angle between the tangents is read from the second-degree part of SS1 = T^2 (the pair-of-lines angle formula), cross-checked by the slope quadratic of the tangents from an external point (way 5). Closest known: angle between the pair of tangents from a point to an ellipse, a standard exercise. Different because: only the numbers are new; the question is deliberately a routine level-2 application in which the two routes must agree. Standard skeleton at L2, flagged honestly.

Checked that P is outside, that no tangent is vertical, and that the formula gives the acute angle (1 + m1 m2 > 0). Changed: No change.
key_step: A = 1/6, B = 1/10, H = -4/15 from SS1 = T^2, then tan theta = 2 sqrt(H^2 - AB)/|A + B|.
justification: Routine application of the pair-of-tangents equation and the angle formula (or Vieta on the slope quadratic); several steps, no insight. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q17 (L2), angle between tangents to ellipses.
blueprint_concepts: tangents drawn from an external point to a Ellipse

concept_use.Pair of tangents for Ellipse: The pair of tangents SS1 = T^2 from P(4,4) gives the second-degree part with A = 1/6, B = 1/10, H = -4/15, whose angle formula gives tan theta = 7/4.
concept_use.tangents drawn from an external point to: The tangents from the external point P(4,4) have slopes satisfying 3m^2 - 16m + 5 = 0; Vieta gives the same tan theta = 7/4 and confirms the angle is acute.
